subject: Cascade Retail — Surge impact analysis, corrective timeline and exec handoff
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cascade-retail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cascade-retail.com
Date: 2027-06-29T21:42:00Z
Subject: sudden throughput surge + errors impacting search checkout

Evelyn / Karthik —

We started seeing a sharp increase in failed inference calls and end-to-end latency around 21:10 UTC. Impact: user checkout calls that hit personalized recommender routes are seeing 10-15% errors (HTTP 502 / 500 range) and 3-4x latency for generation requests. This is affecting a subset of traffic routed to your hosted inference endpoint (model: rwd-mix-13b-v1).

Attached: quick screenshot of errors from our dashboard and the raw throughput CSV for the window (0629 21:05–21:40).

Immediate ask: can you confirm whether any routing changes, model updates, or autoscaler events occurred in that timeframe? We need an ETA for a mitigation path — our checkout conversion is taking a hit.

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Sr. Platform Ops — Cascade Retail

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cascade-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T21:58:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden throughput surge + errors impacting search checkout

Amit —

Thanks for the data and heads up. We're on it. Quick summary of what we see from our side: there was a short-lived spike in request payload size for a subset of keys that triggered a fallback to a higher-memory kernel on the serving pool; combined with a KV-cache miss storm for personalized prefixes this amplified per-token CPU and caused transient OOM retries on a few hosts. No deliberate routing or model push from our control plane at that time.

Immediate mitigations enacted (21:52 UTC):
- Rolled back the temporary kernel affinity that was incorrectly applied to the rwd-mix-13b-v1 variant (reverted kernel binding).
- Applied prefix throttling for affected API route to avoid cascading KV-cache misses while we stabilize.
- Enabled fallback to the 8-bit quantized variant (rwd-mix-13b-v1-q8) for low-priority batch traffic.

Those steps reduced error rates but did not fully restore target latencies. We're standing up a focused bridge for deeper RCA and an exec readout in the morning. I've looped in Karthik and Neha to coordinate remediation and customer comms.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: remediation plan + exec briefing draft for Cascade Retail

Team —

Recap and proposed plan for the morning exec sync with Cascade (09:00 UTC):
1) RCA summary (2 slides): root cause = kernel affinity + KV-cache miss amplification on personalized prefixes leading to host-level retries.
2) Immediate fixes taken: kernel affinity rollback, prefix throttling, q8 fallback. Current status: error rate reduced from ~12% -> ~2.1%, p95 latency down from 1.8s -> 750ms for affected route.
3) Near-term corrective work (proposed 5-day timeline):
   - Day 0–1: thorough host-level heal (drain/restart anti-entropy), increase cache TTL for personalized prefix keys (Neha).
   - Day 1–3: implement rate-aware prefix batching to avoid miss storms; extend autoscaler cooldown tuning (Karthik/Marissa).
   - Day 3–5: release permanent routing policy change with deterministic fallbacks and a hardened kernel affinity gate in the compiler (Jonas).
4) Compensation / contractual next steps: offer 10% credit for impacted token usage window, SLA exception request to be drafted (Evelyn + Legal).

Please review the exec deck draft in the Drive link below; I want bulletized asks and clear owners. We'll also propose a follow-up operational checkpoint at Day 7 to validate metrics and customer satisfaction.

Jonas, can you confirm timeline for kernel affinity gate? Neha, can you scope cache TTL change risk?

-Karthik

Quick updates from infra/compilation:
- Kernel affinity gate: prototype patches are ready; safe rollout can be done within 48–72 hours with feature flag gating. We'll coordinate a canary on the dedicated pool to measure regressions.
- Deterministic fallback: engineering POV is to add a route-level policy that prefers q8 variant + reduced batch sizes under high miss rates; timeline ~3 days for dev + 1 day for canary.

I'll join the 09:00 UTC customer readout for the technical portion.

-Jonas
